newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: New Toyo seeks to expand to increase earnings.
newsitem.headline: New Toyo seeks to expand to increase earnings.

text.p: Paper products and packaging materials maker New Toyo International Holdings Ltd said on Wednesday it looking to expand to increase its earnings.

"Our company is continuously looking for opportunities in the paper industry...in a conscious effort to increase our turnover and profits," Peter Angelakos, New Toyo's chief finance officer told Reuters after a briefing on the company's initial public offer (IPO).
Toyo said on Wednesday it was offering 54 million shares at Singapore S$0.80 each to raise net proceeds of SS$40.2 million.
Angelakos said new plants would be funded by proceeds from the IPO and the company was confident of future growth. He said revenue had risen more than 60 percent in 1996 over 1992.
He said a paper mill being set up in Vietnam to produce toilet and facial tissue would start a new consumer division.

The mill was expected to start operation at the end of 1998 with an initial production of 30 tonnes per day and would contribute to earnings from 1999, Yen Wen Hwa, New Toyo's executive chairman said.
The mill would cater to the Vietnam market, Yen said.
The bulk of New Toyo's revenue and profits are derived from laminated aluminium paper products. Other divisions are non-carbon paper, corrugated carton boxes and trading.
Most of its laminated products are used in the tobacco industry, raising concerns of an over-dependence.

"The group is very dependent on its key customers, namely the British-American Tobacco Group and Vietnam Tobacco Import & Export Co, which accounted for 30.5 percent and 7.2 percnet of group sales in FY1996 respectively," Mano Sabnani, research director of DBS Investment Research said.

Angelakos said the tobacco industry accounted for 72 percent of New Toyo's revenue and 76 of its pretax profits in 1996. This was less than previous years and the company was aiming for equal contributions from all its business areas.
"I expect tobacco to contribute in the region of 20 percent to revenue in about five years," Angelakos said.
According to the company's prospectus, New Toyo has developed new applications for its laminated products -- for packaging food, beverage and cosmetics -- to broaden its customer base.
For the fiscal year ended December 31, 1996, New Toyo recorded a net profit of S$10.08 million on a turnover of S$127.4 million.
Two new plants to be built in China and Burma would double capacity for corrugated carton boxex from the current 1,500 tonne per month when they were ready in 1998, Angelakos said.
New Toyo presently has 10 plants in Asia and Australia, seven of which are for laminated products.

On its non-carbon products business, which turned in a loss of Singapore $0.9 million in 1996, Angelakos said the company had consolidated the operations in Malaysia to lower costs and for economies of scale. He expected the division to be profitable in 1997.
